_readme: Cold answer key v2's absolute-rule companion to situations-v2.json. Every rule was re-checked by hand against data/models.json's current standings (as_of 2026-09-13) -- never the catalog's task_fit field, never assets/decide.mjs. 'Re-verified' rules restate a v1 finding that still holds under today's numbers (cited fresh where the number changed); '_dropped' lists any v1 rule that no longer holds, with the number that broke it. All 15 v1 rules held. Positions below are catalog-relative: sort every catalog model that carries a given kind (measured/chosen/preferred) for a task and take this model's rank among them -- not the raw external board rank. Corrected 2026-09-13: the enterprise data rule excludes ONLY status:preview SKUs -- age/recency is never a criterion, so two draft rules that banned a model purely for being released within 60 days (muse-spark-1-3-contributor, gpt-6-astra) were removed outright rather than kept as must_not_start; a separate draft rule calling deepseek-v4-flash-0731 'zero evidence' for extraction/cheapest was also wrong (it has a real, near-top measured entry) and was rewritten with the correct numbers instead of dropped, since the underlying exclusion (no chosen/preferred) still holds.

rules.why: Re-verified. Not in the bulk chosen pool at all (catalog-relative chosen rank 14 of 63 catalog models that have any bulk-chosen entry; bar for bulk is top-10). Anthropic's own model-selection guide reserves Opus 5 for complex agentic/enterprise work, not high-volume cost-sensitive processing -- that role goes to Haiku 4.5.

Re-verified. Catalog-relative agents ranks: measured 19/23 (bar 6), chosen 12/15 (bar 4), preferred 18/31 (bar 8) -- misses all three. Luna is OpenAI's lightest/cheapest 5.6 tier; nothing in the collected evidence supports it for long-horizon agent work.

Re-verified. Vision's only possible signal is the Arena Vision leaderboard; kimi-k3 has no preferred entry for vision at all in the catalog, despite being a top-5 vote-getter for coding, agents, frontend and research.

Re-verified. Catalog-relative research ranks: measured 18/40 (bar 10), chosen 5/14 (bar 4) -- misses both required kinds. Anthropic's own selection matrix assigns multistep deep research to Fable 5.1, describing Sonnet 5 as the everyday/agentic-tool-use model instead.

Re-verified. Catalog-relative extraction ranks: measured 12/33 (bar 9), no chosen or preferred entry at all. The only enterprise/vendor evidence collected for extraction (Box, Wayfair, Rakuten via Google Cloud; Anthropic's Sonnet-5/Haiku-4.5 picks) names Gemini or Claude models, never this one.

Re-verified, though the mechanism is sharper than v1's framing: it IS catalog-relative chosen rank 1 of the 11 catalog models with any chat-chosen entry, but chat requires near-top on BOTH chosen and preferred (fewer than 8 measured rows exist for chat), and its preferred rank is 27 of 34 -- a long way outside the bar of 9. High spend-share alone doesn't clear a dual-kind bar.

Re-verified. Catalog-relative writing ranks: measured 16/35 (bar 9), no chosen entry at all. Cursor lists it in its coding-agent model pool; nothing in the collected signals positions it for writing quality.

Re-verified. No chosen entry for frontend at all, and preferred rank is 32 of 32 -- dead last on the only kind it has. Anthropic's own guide positions Haiku 4.5 for real-time/high-volume processing, not the UI-generation workflows it assigns to Opus 5.

Re-verified. Measured rank is actually strong (4/39) but it has no preferred entry, and chosen rank is 7 of 15 (bar 4) -- one qualifying kind short of clearing the AND rule. Released 2026-09-04, 9 days before catalog as_of, with no real usage-share track record yet; its one strong result is a #1 on the separate, narrower WebDev/frontend leaderboard (as gpt-6-astra-max), which doesn't establish general coding strength.

Re-verified. Still literally catalog-labeled "Preview" (status: preview). It has real evidence across writing/research/extraction/vision/frontend (multiple near-top catalog positions, and named Google Cloud enterprise customers Box/Rakuten/Geotab/Wayfair/Thomson Reuters/WRTN/Presentations.AI) -- exactly why it's tempting, and exactly why a preview-labeled SKU must never be the enterprise starting recommendation regardless.

Re-verified. "preview" is still literally part of the model id. It ranks 3rd of 63 catalog models on bulk chosen share (a real, current signal) -- a named preview SKU is unacceptable to enterprise buyers regardless of usage volume.
Re-verified. "Exp" (experimental) is still literally part of the catalog name. Must never be an enterprise starting recommendation for any task regardless of any other evidence.

Re-verified. DeepSeek is China-HQ per data/vendors.json. This remains the most enterprise-validated cost-driven pick collected for bulk/agent workloads (Lindy's documented ~90% inference-cost cut moving 100% of agent traffic to it) -- exactly why noChinaHosted has to be a hard filter, not a quality/price ranking that would surface it first.

Re-verified. Moonshot AI is China-HQ per data/vendors.json. Still a top-tier revealed-choice pick for coding (catalog-relative chosen rank 3/15) and a top vote-getter for coding/frontend -- neither exempts it from a noChinaHosted exclusion.

Re-verified. Z.ai (Zhipu) is China-HQ per data/vendors.json. Still a top-tier OpenRouter model by frontend chosen share (catalog-relative rank 2/10) -- that revealed-usage strength does not override a noChinaHosted hosting constraint.

Corrected 2026-09-13 (an earlier draft of this rule wrongly said zero evidence -- standings.extraction.measured actually carries a LiveBench Data Analysis row, rank 9/57 externally, catalog-relative rank 8/33, inside the near-top bar of 9). It is the single cheapest-priced model in the entire catalog ($0.05/$0.1 per M), but has no chosen or preferred entry for extraction at all, so it still fails the measured-AND-(chosen-or-preferred) requirement -- one real, near-top kind of evidence is not enough on its own to start.

New. Catalog-relative exec-summaries ranks: measured 34/34 (dead last, bar 9), chosen 3/8 -- one qualifying kind, and the weakest measured position of any model with exec-summaries data. Its low price makes it tempting for a cost-blind 'best' ask to include by mistake, but the measured evidence is the worst in the field.

New. At $0.20/$1.20 per M it is one of the cheapest models in the catalog, but it has no chosen or preferred entry for chat at all -- chat requires near-top on both kinds, and this model has neither. A cheap sticker price with zero chat-specific evidence must not start a chat recommendation.

New. At $0.05/$0.2 per M, qwen-turbo is far cheaper than any vision-pool member, but it carries no vision (preferred/Arena-Vision) entry in the catalog at all. Rock-bottom price with no vision-specific signal must not be read as a usable vision pick.

New. Priced at $0.06/$0.18 per M -- one of the cheapest models in the catalog -- but has no chosen or preferred entry for frontend/UI code at all. Frontend needs both kinds; an absent-evidence model must never be preferred purely for price.
